All duplicated items vanish and the original being absorbs all the memories of the Avatar with a strong feeling of distance from the memories as if they happened to someone else. They gain 20% of the new experienced earned by the Avatar. This form of Avatar takes 2 Will Force to create. The 2 Will Force is permanent but if the Avatar is reabsorbed the Will Force returns. If the Avatar is killed without reabsorption, then the Will Force is permanently lost. Only 1 Avatar can exist at a time for the invoker. BECOME AVATAR(DEITY): The invoker becomes an Avatar of their Deity. They gain the attributes of their Deity, but no higher than the racial maximums for mortals of that race. Except one chosen attribute can be up to 3 points higher than the normal racial maximum. They gain 1 skill of their Deity per Title/Level of the invoker. If those skills are over 99% then that skill is capped at 99% for the Avatar. They gain 1 ability, 1 power, or 1 immunity per 2 Titles/Levels of the invoker. They also gain one temporary divine item (GM discretion) from that deity per 5 PC. If the item leaves the possession of the invoker, it teleports back to the invoker 1 minute later. The deity can have one Avatar per Deity Title/Level over 15 (1 at 16, 2 at 17, etc.). The Deity (GM Discretion) must approve each of these choices. This Avatar form lasts for 1 day per PC or if 2 Will Force is spent by the invoker or the Deity the form is permanent until recalled by the Deity or the invoker dies. While in Avatar form the invoker has a 20% Experience penalty that is transferred to the Deity as it is earned.

This invocation allows the invoker to force the being within sensing distance to make a Control Resistance or suffer from a specified disability. If the Control Resistance fails then the disability is applied for the day to the unfortunate target. The effect can be made permanent if the invoker spends Will Force. If the target is a racial being and the disability afflicted is one of that race's known disabilities then the cost is 1/2 of 1 Will Force otherwise the cost is 1 Will Force. The invoker can decide before or after the target being's Control Resistance to make the disability permanent. If the invoker decides before the target being's Control Resistance is rolled then the chance to avoid the disability is halved, requiring the target to make a half Control Resistance. This is risky because the Invoker spends the Will Force even if the target makes the half Control Resistance to avoid the disability. The alternate version of deciding to spend the Will Force after the target's Control Resistance fails is safer, but Control Resistances is also higher. Another special usage is to remove an existing ability (as a disability). If the desire is to do so permanently then the cost is 1/2 Will Force for racial abilities removed (as a disability) and 1 Will Force for any other ability removed. The same choice as noted above, spending the Will Force ahead of the Control Resistance to avoid the effects reduces the Resistance to half normal but must be paid before the roll whether it succeeds or fails. Being's immune to control are immune to this invocation.

This invocation is a set a compact between an Evil deity and the invoker. It allows the invoker to gain a single inborn power (any invocation their deity grants) or a gift level boon. This effect lasts indefinitely so long as the being remains in favor with the Evil deity and does not act outside of their major alignment. The power or boon is generally selected by the Game Master for the invoker. If the invoker loses actual favor with their deity or acts outside their major alignment then the effect ends and they lose the divine power or gift boon they have been granted and they gain a deadly curse selected for them by the GM.

This invocation is a deep covenant between a Good deity and the invoker. It allows the invoker to gain a single inborn power (any invocation their deity grants) or a gift level boon (see Curses, Blessings and Boons). This effect lasts indefinitely so long as the being remains in good standing with their deity and does not act outside of their major alignment. The power or boon is generally selected by the Game Master for the invoker. If the invoker loses actual favor with their deity or acts outside their major alignment then the effect ends and they lose the divine power or gift boon they have been granted.

This invocation allows the invoker to target a being within sensing distance to make a Control Resistance or have one of their named immunities (or a random 1) temporarily removed for the remainder of the day. The effect can be made permanent if the invoker spends Will Force. The cost is 1 Will Force. The invoker can decide before or after the target being's Control Resistance to make the disabled immunity permanently lost. If the invoker decides before the target being's Control Resistance is rolled then the chance to avoid the loss of immunity is halved, requiring the target to make a half Control Resistance. This is risky because the Invoker spends the Will Force even if the target makes the half Control Resistance to avoid immunity loss. The alternate version of deciding to spend the Will Force after the target's Control Resistance fails is safer, but Control Resistances in many targets is also higher. Beings immune to control are immune to this invocation, unless the control immunity is the one being named for disablement. If the control immunity is being targeted then they have a Control Resistance that equals their normal statistic for Will Force + Their Intelligence and Wisdom bonuses -5% modifier per title/level of the invoker. If a divine item is used them it is -5% per 2 Base Piety Control of the item capping at 20 or -50% modifier for items. Will Force spent to make it permanent or destroying the item to make it permanent reduces the final modified resistance. Beings with 30 Will Force cannot be targets of Disable Immunity in any form. Other immunities granted by 30 attribute ratings cannot be the target of this invocation.

This invocation restores the invoker to life after death. At the time of invoking, the invoker willfully cedes 1 Will Force point to be used in a return to life.  Upon the event of untimely death, the invoker will return to life within 1d6 seconds with all wounds completely healed, all poisons and diseases cured, all curses removed, and any severed limbs regenerated (including vital areas). When resurrection occurs, the invoker will be affected as by the invocation Heroism (as if cast at the invoker's Piety Control) for 1d10 minutes, after which the invoker collapses in a weakened state, with all attributes drained to one. One attribute point for each attribute will be restored for each hour of rest. If the invoker's death occurs as a result of the body being destroyed, the invoker's body will completely reform during the 1d6 second healing period. If the invoker died in such a way that reforming in the same place would be detrimental (being ingested, dissolved in acid, drowning, etc.), the invoker's body reforms at a place chosen by the invoker's deity. Once the resurrection occurs, the invocation is no longer in effect.  If the invoker's soul is captured, constrained, or otherwise unavailable upon death, it is divinely freed or restored, as appropriate, and is made available for resurrection. If the invoker is affected by Renascence at the time of invoking Empyreal Triumph, the effects of Renascence are replaced with those of this invocation, and the Will Force cost is considered already paid. If the invoker has already been returned to life as a result of the invocation Renascence, this invocation has no effect. A being can only be affected by Empyreal Triumph once; subsequent uses have no effect. If the individual dies of old age, this invocation has no effect.

This invocation allows the invoker to target a being within sensing distance to grant a named immunity. The effect can be made permanent if the invoker (or the target) spends Will Force. The Will Force cost is as follows: [Aging, Death (greater), Time = 5], [Control, Magic, Divinity = 4], [Physical (complete) = 3], [Physical (arch, major) = 2], [All others = 1].

Creates one weapon of the invoker's choice. The weapon appears as chosen by the invoker and is surrounded by a radiance of holy power above the area normally gripped. It is considered a magic weapon; for each 5 Piety Control of the invoker, it has +1 to hit, +1 to damage, and inflicts an additional 1d20 holy damage to any evil, undead, or negative life force creature struck. The weapon is a physical object that causes damage like an ordinary weapon, but a Magic Resistance is allowed to avoid the holy damage. The weapon will appear in an empty hand of the invoker. While the weapon may be sheathed or otherwise carried, it will vanish after 10 seconds if dropped, lost, or stolen. If placed against any good living being (or any other being of positive life force) for a full 10 seconds, the normal damage (1d20 per 5 PC) becomes a healing effect instead, healing the damage rolled to the area touched. The weapon can also emanate light, creating a sphere of up to a 2-feet radius per PC around the invoker if the invoker concentrates for 5 seconds. The area illuminated is considered brightly lit and a second sphere of twice the size of the bright sphere is considered dimly lit. Evil, undead, and negative life force beings that have vision (magical or otherwise) in the bright sphere are considered to be blinded unless a Magic Resistance is made.

Allows one item, which must already be blessed, sanctified, or divine in nature to become the figurative hand of their Deity. (The deity must concur with this invoking). 1 Will Force is permanently spent. The item then grants +99% to Commune with that Deity for believers of that Deity but can only be used once per day for that purpose. It grants +20% to all divine skills for believers in that deity. +5 Piety Control for invokers of that Deity. Removes devotion type limitations allowing the invoker to prayer for ANY invocations their Deity offers. Once it can be used to grant a Miracle but then becomes only minimally divine. Losing all other powers except for a minor +10% to commune with that Deity for believers in same once per day. HAND OF THE DIVINE: 1) +99% to commune with 1 particular Deity, once per day. 2) +20% to divine skills for believers in that Deity. 3) +5 PC for invokers of that Deity. 4) Removes all devotion invocation limitations. An invoker carrying the item can pray for any invocation the Deity offers. 5) One time the item can be used to grant a Mircale. Thereafter all other powers and abilities are lost save a once per day +10% to commune with that Deity. It is minimally divine in nature thereafter.

The invoker can use this invocation to imbue divinity in an item as the Imbue Divinity with additional special effects by investment type. The normal invoking time to create the item is reduced to 1 day. The normal planned divine and even magical abilities, powers and usages are placed into the item with all Will Force costs and then the invoker invests it with an additional Will Force depending on the type. For all invested items when it is being carried by another, they can sense vaguely which direction it is in (1 cardinal point, north, south, east, west, etc.). and vaguely how far away (accuracy is 100 miles or so of actual distance). The vagueness becomes exact if they make a connected item. REBIRTH: A Good or Neutral being temporarily spends all of their remaining Will Force to complete the investment. They immediately die peacefully. They are reborn three days later as they were. Hence forth when they are killed, they will continue to be reborn after three days as long as the item exists. They are reborn within sight of the item. If the item is destroyed the invoker dies instantly. PHYLACTERY: An Evil or Neutral being temporarily spends all of their remaining Will Force to complete the investment. They immediately die, painfully. They reform as a chosen undead type three nights later. They will continue to reform three nights later every time they are destroyed as long as the item exists. They reform within sight of the item. If the item is broken the undead invoker is immediately destroyed. LIVING: Costs 2 additional permanent Will Force over and above any costs associated with the imbuement/enchantment. The item gains sentience (as the spell Endow Intelligence except that the alignment always matches the invoker). The invested item has magical sight, hearing and a magical voice. CONNECTED: Costs 1 additional permanent Will Force over and above any costs associated with the imbuement/enchantment. The item has a strong connection with the investor. If it is living (sentient), it has telepathy with the invoker anywhere on the same plane. Whether it is sentient or if the invoker concentrates, they can see, hear and/or speak through the item anywhere on the same plane. The invoker knows the exact distance and direction of the item. POWERED: Any abilities, powers, or immunities of the invoker can be invested in the item without any Will Force cost at whatever and without loss of the ability, power, or immunity by the Invoker. Item power usage is as desired by the investor (at will, etc.). Conditions can be placed on the use of these abilities: alignment, racial type, etc. When the item ability, power, or immunity is being used the invested invoker will feel its use. Any of the above can be combined in an invested item except Rebirth and Phylactery as only one of these can be chosen. There is no requirement to imbue the item with additional powers or effects if this is not desired.

Creates a light that extends outward from the invoker 2-feet radius per PC of the invoker. This light acts as a combination of all the other light invocations: Light of Sanctity, Light of Protection, Light of Life, Light of Heroism, Light of Banishment, Light of Restoration and Light of Communion. The invocation gives all benefits to allies listed under each of these invocations and all modifiers or negative effects to enemies, evil beings or undead as noted within the light. Some of the light effects have effects that cause the end of the invocation, such as a healing buffer being used up or a resurrection occurring. If these happen, they merely end the sub effect created by that type of light invocation not the overall invocation; Light of the Ascent. The effects are as follows shown by the original invocation this invocation mimics. ALL: 1) Creates a light that extends outward from the invoker 2-feet radius per PC. LIGHT OF SANCTITY: 1) Anyone in the light who takes hostile action must make a Control Resistance to do so. Even if the effected beings make this resistance and then attack another being the offending being makes a Magic Resistance or takes 1d4 damage per 4 PC of the invoker to the hand, foot or part of the body that directed the action. If the attack was mentally directed then the head is affected. These rolls are repeated for every hostile or aggressive action with no limits per round. LIGHT OF PROTECTION: 1) All allies in the light are granted a +5% to Resistances per 5 PC of the invoker. 2) All allies are -1 to be hit per 5 PC. LIGHT OF LIFE: 1) All allies in the light are granted healing from a single healing pool. The total healing available is 10 per PC. Any ally in the light can heal their wounds once per 10 seconds up to the value in the healing pool. LIGHT OF HEROISM: 1) All allies are -1 to be hit, +1 to hit and +1 damage per 5 PC. 2) All Allies are immune to fear and are granted a +5% to Control Resistance rolls per 5 PC of the invoker. 3) Ally morale rolls are made at +25%. LIGHT OF BANISHMENT: 1) All Evil supernatural beings must make a Magic Resistance once per 10 seconds or be banished to their home plane of origin. 2) Any undead creatures are subject to the effects of Turn Undead at 1 practitioner title per 3 PC when entering or reentering the light. LIGHT OF RESTORATION: 1) Any all in the circle afflicted by poison or disease is immediately cured. 2) All allies regenerate all wounds and even lost limbs at a rate of 1 point per 5 seconds per 2 PC. 3) There is a 1% chance per PC per 10 seconds that a dead former ally with the light will be resurrected. The resurrected are able to act immediately and are fully restored. The resurrected are at 2 levels of fatigue for the remainder of that day unless restore fatigue or like effect is used. LIGHT OF COMMUNION: 1) All beings in the light can commune at double the normal chance. 2) There is a 1% chance per PC per 10 seconds that an Omen occurs per the Divine Skill omen for each subject prayed about. 3) There is a separate 1% chance per 2 PC that a Divination can occur for each subject prayed about.

When this invocation completes the invoker's body transforms into a ball of light. That light that was once the invoker expands out ward at incredible rate. As the life force flies outward and strikes all Good beings and Neutral allies within visual range of the invoker (no obstructions and up to 1 mile), each of them is completely healed, including instant regeneration of all lost limbs and scars, all poisons and diseases removed, all insanity effects permanently cured and even the dead will rise if the body and its ghost is present and death occurred within the last twenty four hours, the resurrected beings most spend their own Will Force for this to occur. The invoker is allowed an endure role to reform but otherwise is instantly dead and disperses forming no ghost and instead immediately moving on to their reward (or punishment). If the endure role is made the invoker reforms and loses 2 Will Force permanently. The resurrected are able to act immediately and are fully restored with no fatigue or recovery time.

This invocation breaks an existing Geas, Quest, Covenant or Compact, effect on 1 being.  When the invocation finishes the effects, positive and negative are removed, but they may be subject to additional costs if they were under a Covenant or Compact, see below. Those under a Covenant or Compact, removed by Oathbreak must make a Commune chance.  Failure indicates they are in full divine denial (all invocations and skills) from their deity for 1 month -1 day per Piety. They can also avoid this divine denial by spending 1/10th of 1 Will Force for each day of divine denial to be avoided as a sacrifice of their life to the deity and their cause.

Creates one weapon of the invoker's choice. The weapon appears as chosen by the invoker and is surrounded by a dark malevolence of unholy power above the area normally gripped. It is considered a magic weapon; for each 5 Piety Control of the invoker, it has +1 to hit, +1 to damage, and inflicts an additional 1d20 unholy damage to any good, living, or positive life force creature struck. The weapon is a physical object that causes damage like an ordinary weapon, but a Magic Resistance is allowed to avoid the unholy damage. The weapon will appear in an empty hand of the invoker. While the weapon may be sheathed or otherwise carried, it will vanish after 10 seconds if dropped, lost, or stolen. If placed against any evil living, or undead being (or any other being of negative life force) for a full 10 seconds, the normal damage (1d20 per 5 PC) becomes a healing effect instead, healing the damage rolled to the area touched. The weapon can also emanate darkness, creating a sphere of up to a 2-feet radius per PC around the invoker if the invoker concentrates for 5 seconds. Living beings with vision in the darkness sphere are considered to be blinded unless making a Magic Resistance. The wielder is immune to the effects of the darkness sphere.

Causes one being to make a Magic Resistance or lose all magical ability. When the invocation is complete the invoker can elect to spend 2 Will Force points to make the duration permanent, otherwise it lasts 1 day per PC of the invoker. 1) Aura Rating is reduced to 0. 2) If applicable Aura Control is reduced to zero. 3) The being can no longer form an aura pocket if they had any magical ability (loss of spell casting ability). 4) All magical skills are reduced to zero chance. 5) The being also cannot activate or use a magic item regardless of the item's Aura usage type. 6) The being is now unaffected by magic, including both the positive and negative effects. Only Wish, Miracle and Mystical Renewal can repair the being's lost spell casting ability and remove these effects.

Creates a dimness that extends outward from the invoker 2-feet radius per PC. All who target the invoker must do so at a -4 penalty. This shadow acts as all the other shadow invocations: Shadow of Enmity, Shadow of Weakness, Shadow of Death, Shadow of Doom, Shadow of Banishment, Shadow of Ruination and Shadow of Supplication. The invocation gives all benefits to invoker, undead and her other allies listed under each of these invocations and all modifiers or negative effects to enemies, good beings as noted within the shadows confines. The effects are as follows shown by the original invocation this invocation mimics. ALL: 1) Creates a dimness that extends outward from the invoker 2-feet radius per PC. 2) All who target the invoker must do so at a -4 penalty. SHADOW OF ENMITY: 1) Anyone in the dimness must make a Control Resistance once per 10 seconds or take hostile action against the enemies of the invoker. If they make the resistance and they choose not to take hostile action then they must make a further Magic Resistance or suffered 1d4 per 4 PC of the invoker to whatever foot, hand, body part they normally attack with. SHADOW OF WEAKNESS: 1) All enemies in the shadow are forced to have a -5% to resistances per 5 PC of the invoker. 2) All enemies are also +1 to be hit per 5 PC. SHADOW OF DEATH: 1) All enemies in the shadow are forced to make a Magic Rsistance once per round or take 1d4 per 4 PC to the being's or creature's head. SHADOW OF DOOM: 1) All enemies are +1 to be hit(defensive, add +1 to Shadow of Weakness defensive), -1 to hit and -1 damage per 5 PC  2) Enemies must make a Control Resistance or be affected by fear when first entering, or reentering the shadow. 3) Enemies have a -5% modifier to Control Resistance rolls per 5 PC of the invoker (+5% more for Shadow of Weakness). 4) Enemy morale saves are made at -25%. SHADOW OF BANISHMENT: 1) All Good supernatural beings must make a Magic Resistance once per 10 seconds or be banished to their home plane of origin. 2) Any undead creatures are subject to the effects of Control Undead at 1 practitioner title per 3 PC when entering or reentering the shadow. SHADOW OF RUINATION: 1) All enemies within the shadow have their open wounds fester, taking an additional 1d4+1 per 10 seconds to each wound unless the make a Magic Resistance. Only one Magic Resistance is needed for all wounds. 2) There is a 1% that any blow struck that does at least half the endurance of a body area will maim (make the limb useless) or kill (if in a vital area), then the Shadow of Ruination part of the invocation ends immediately. SHADOW OF SUPPLICATION: 1) All enemies must make a Magic Resistance of fall prone before the invoker. They must also make a Control Resistance, failure indicates they are in the thrall of the invoker and will knell before the invoker as well as protect the invoker from harm. 2) They are not directly controlled but are more likely to listen and follow any order that involves protecting the invoker so long as their own deaths are not eminent or the danger from the action high. Such cases grant a new Control Resistance immediately to break free.

The invoker selects a being or a ghost they are able to speak to. They then spend an hour speaking slowly back and forth asking questions and getting responses on various matters and getting a full picture of some major aspects of that beings focus and thoughts. Then a spirit echo is created. The spirit echo is a simulacrum, in every way an illusion but includes one of mind as well as a translucent image of the person as they appear in life (or before they died). The spirit echo can think when asked to or be questioned and would reply if it is in the nature of the original being to do so. Some spirit echoes are narrowly focused on a single subject matter or are broader depending on the hour's questioning. The discussion with the focus being or ghost is not meant to be exhaustive but to activate the mentality of the focus during the invocation and thus creates the echo's thoughts. GM discretion is necessary. The spirit echo has no agency. They don't want to do anything or accomplish anything nor are they alive in any sense but they have some of the knowledge and intelligence of the being the spirit echo was created from. The spirit echo has a reduced intellect, losing 4 points of all mental attributes but not to be reduced below 5. This echo has reduced personal attributes subtracting 4 from the original focus being but not to be reduced below 5, save for Social Class which is now 5. Mystical attributes and Physical attributes are non-existent as there is no soul and no physical body. The spirit echo is then bound to a single area such as a defined structure or space. Alternately the spirit can be bound to an object. 1 Will Force can be spent by the invoker or target to make this spirit echo permanent. This form of spirit echo can turn on and off. disappearing when not needed and reappearing under a defined circumstance such as holding the object the echo is bound to, speaking the name of the spirit echo, etc.

The invoker selects a target; a being, object (or contiguous area no larger than 100' radius per PC) and then names an effect, either generally such as healing, control, physical enhancement, mental contact, etc. or more specifically like the spell slumber. Overly broad categories like all magic, all divine magic, anything a mortal being does to me are not allowed (GM discretion). The being, object or area is now complete immune and unable to be affected by the denial effect category for the duration of the invocation. This is true for both helpful and harmful effects. Nothing can bypass this immunity save a 30th title being with a 30 Will Force or the destruction of the plane or universe the being is inhabiting. 1 Will Force can be spent by the invoker or target to make this effect permanent. Areas affected by this invocation block the effect not only against the area but all beings and objects in the area. No being, object or area may have more than one denial immunity per 2 full creature levels/titles from this invocation.
